description: Average the customer counts over every employee, with employees who have no customers counted as zero.

d.request: For each employee, count assigned customers, treating employees with none as zero, then calculate the average count across all employees without rounding.
d.sql:
SELECT AVG(customer_count) AS average_customer_count
FROM (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS customer_count
  FROM Employee e
  LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
) AS employee_customer_counts;

a.request: Counting, for every employee, the customers whose `SupportRepId` is that employee (zero for employees with none), what is the average number of customers per employee? Don't round.
a.sql:
SELECT AVG(customer_count) AS average_customers_per_employee
FROM (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS customer_count
  FROM Employee e
  LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
) AS employee_customer_counts;

c.request: On average, how many customers does each support rep look after? Don't round. Average the customer counts over every employee, with employees who have no customers counted as zero.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(customer_count) FROM (SELECT e.EmployeeId, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS customer_count FROM Employee e LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId) AS employee_customer_counts;
